title: Cloud networking: VPC, subnets, security groups and load balancers

videos.script: You start a virtual machine in the cloud, and it gets an address. Where does that address come from, and who else can reach it? {{address}} Behind every machine in lesson 4 there is a network nobody showed you. The provider lets you draw it yourself. It is called a virtual private cloud, a VPC, and the range of addresses inside it is yours to choose. {{vpc}} In this lesson you carve that range into subnets, with a little arithmetic you can check on a laptop. Then you see that a subnet is public because of one line in its route table. It is not a switch somebody turned on. {{routes}} Then come the filters. A security group sits on each machine and remembers the conversations it let in. A network ACL sits on the whole subnet and remembers nothing. {{filters}} A load balancer puts one address in front of many machines, and stops sending traffic to the ones that died. Put all of it together and you get the layout most applications run on: three tiers, in two zones. {{layout}} And when a machine cannot be reached, you will have a checklist, in order. The symptom tells you where to start. None of this needs an account. Every price comes from the public list, and every number can be worked out again. {{checklist}}
